title: Abort decision within time bound
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let $L$ be a language of finite Boolean strings, and let $T$ assign a natural-number time bound to each natural number. For every input string $x$, every run halts within $T(|x|)$ steps; every choice string of length exactly $T(|x|)$ produces an output different from the one-symbol answer indicating whether $x$ belongs to $L$; and the probability that the output after $T(|x|)$ steps is that one-symbol answer is at least $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
